speaker: Mr Speaker
text: In accordance with the decision of the House to have a simultaneous debate on both Motions, I will now call on Members to make their speeches.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Members are allowed to consider both Motions in a single speech.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: The time limits will apply as if it were a debate on a single Motion.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: At the end of the debate, I will put the questions on both Motions to a vote, so that the House can express its views on each Motion separately.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Any Member who disagrees with a Motion can vote against that Motion.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: (In Mandarin):   Mr Speaker, I support my colleague Ms Hazel Poa's Motion today.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The Progressive Singapore Party (PSP), tabling this Motion today, that is of historic significance, which is to uphold the zero-tolerance approach that our nation has towards corruption.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: For many years, the People's Action Party (PAP) government has been telling Singaporeans we must provide high pay to Ministers and Parliamentarians in order to ensure that the Government maintains its fairness and incorruptibility.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The PSP agrees with paying people well to maintain corruptibility, but we also believe that when a Minister or Parliamentarian is being investigated for corruption and when this investigation or criminal case has not been ended yet, they should be suspended from their duties, or they should stop receiving such high pay for the time being.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: If the Parliamentarian or Minister were to be decided to be acquitted and to be guilt-free, then the full amount of the pay due to him during the unpaid leave period should be paid back.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The Leader of the House, Ms Indranee Rajah, today also raised a Motion and it requires that Parliament awaits the result of Minister Iswaran's case to be out before we make a decision on this.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The Government has the responsibility to prudently use the taxpayers' money and it has the obligation to prevent taxpayers' money from being abused or misused.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: To that end, the PSP disagrees with the Motion from the Leader of the House and is unable to agree or accept that arrangement.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The PSP believes that if Minister Iswaran is eventually found to be not guilty of corruption, then taxpayers, due to the restrictions of the current laws, would not be able to recover or claw back the money that has been paid out.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: But if we do not claw it back, that means that taxpayers, during the period through which a person is being investigated of a corruption have, for no reason, paid a large sum of money to this person under corruption charges.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We are talking about a sum of $16,000 per month.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: From the Ministry of Manpower, we can understand that there are so many Singaporeans who are working diligently and contributing their labour and effort, and, despite that, their household income is below that of $16,000.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Of course, the PSP also wants to seriously proclaim that we believe that before Minister Iswaran is proven to be guilty by the Court, he is innocent.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Suspending his duties and allowance are but temporary.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: If he is found to be not guilty eventually, then we should, when the whole investigation is completed, repay him the MP allowance.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The PSP would like to say that for taxpayers and Minister Iswaran, there should be a fair approach.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: And that is why we are tabling this Motion today to suspend his duties and MP allowance for the time being.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The PSP has tabled this Motion for the for the amendment Bill because we truly want to improve our system, and this is valid, reasonable and in accordance with the laws.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We hope that all Parliamentarians can understand our intention and provide full support.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: (In English): I support the Motion moved by Ms Hazel Poa.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: First, let me speak on the issue of fairness.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: The hon Member Ms Hazel Poa's case is that a Member should be suspended from Parliament because he has been arrested and is being investigated for the serious offence of corruption.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: However, the centrality of the rule of law in Singapore renders the hon Member's suggested course of action premature, a point made all the more stark because we do not even know the details of what Mr S Iswaran is accused of.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Parliament should be mindful of the dictum of presumption of innocence.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: With respect, I would also request PSP colleagues in the House to consider the precedent their Motion would create should a future government decide to fix Opposition MPs by way of politically motivated investigations.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: In a few other cases, accused persons who have been brought to trial have been acquitted or the prosecution applies to withdraw the charges.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: In yet other cases, those convicted at first instance have seen their convictions overturned on appeal.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Any of these scenarios could come to pass in Mr Iswaran's case.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: In the Workers' Party's (WP) view, the wheels of justice must be allowed to fully turn before Parliament decides what to do.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: It would not just be unfair and premature but, significantly, this House would be seeking to overturn the electoral mandate given to Mr Iswaran by the people through the ballot box by prematurely passing judgement on him.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: This leads me to the second issue on how to deal with an MP who has been put by his party leader on indeterminate leave of absence from Parliament with full MP's allowance.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: WP MP Mr Dennis Tan raised this matter of Mr Iswaran's MP allowance in Parliament last month.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: As far as I know, Mr Iswaran is neither performing duties in his constituency nor in Parliament and his likeness is not found on Town Council or People's Association banners in West Coast Group Representation Constituency (GRC).

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: The Prime Minister said in this House last month that if Parliament wants to stop an MP's allowance, Parliament has to move to interdict the individual as an MP and Parliament has not done that and, I quote, "What has happened is that the MP has been on a leave of absence and, eventually, when the case is settled in one way or another, then consequences would follow." What needs to be noted, however, is that the Prime Minister's act of interdicting Mr Iswaran as Minister appears to have effectively interdicted him as an MP as well.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: For the WP to decide on whether to support the Leader's Motion, there are a few questions I would like to ask the Leader in order that this House can understand the full extent of the restrictions on Mr Iswaran as an MP.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: My first question is: can the Leader confirm whether Mr Iswaran's ban on entering Government buildings extends to Parliament House?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Does Mr Iswaran have access to the Public Service Division's MP Appeal System and is he rendering assistance or expected to do so to his residents in his capacity as an MP?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: My second question addresses the Prime Minister's comment that consequences will follow.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: It is unclear if those, I quote, "consequences" include a clawback of the MP allowance.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: For completeness, it is this issue that forms the basis of my Parliamentary Question today and filed on 7 September about the duration Mr Iswaran is expected to be absent from Parliament.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: My third question concerns para (c) of the Leader's Motion where it says that this House will consider this matter when the outcome of ongoing investigations is known.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: This contrasts with what the Prime Minister said during the clarifications of the Prime Minister's Ministerial Statement on Mr Iswaran last month.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: The Prime Minister said and, I quote, "If there is a case, the case has not been heard, he has not been found guilty or acquitted or whatever." My third question is this: can the Leader clarify whether the word "outcome" in para (c) of the Leader's Motion means that this House will consider this matter once investigations are completed and a decision has been made on whether charges would be preferred against Mr Iswaran or if it means that this House will consider this matter only upon conclusion of the entire criminal justice process, including any possible appeal?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: The WP's position on the Leader's Motion will turn on the responses to these three specific queries.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: The burden of proof is placed on the prosecution, and the accused is assumed to be innocent until the prosecution can prove beyond reasonable doubt that the defendant is guilty of the crime that he has been charged with.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: The accused does not even need to prove his innocence.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: The burden of proof is on the prosecution.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: This principle is also enshrined in the United Nation's Universal Declaration of Human Rights.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: At Article 11, it says: "Everyone charged with a penal offence has the right to be presumed innocent until proved guilty according to law in a public trial at which he has had all the guarantees necessary for his defence.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: No one shall be held guilty of any penal offence on account of any act or omission which did not constitute a penal offence, under national or international law, at the time when it was committed.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Nor shall a heavier penalty be imposed than the one that was applicable at the time that the penal offence was committed." Sir, to the best of my knowledge, Mr Iswaran is currently under investigations by CPIB.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: He has not been charged for an offence and neither has he been convicted in a Court of law of any offence.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: CPIB would need to interview Minister Iswaran to take the investigation further and he sought my concurrence to open a formal investigation.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I instructed him to take leave of absence until the investigations were completed." Sir, to this date, I am not aware of any other facts that have come out and the Prime Minister had said that CPIB investigations are still ongoing.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: He said, "Details cannot be provided so as not to prejudice the investigations." Thus, if Ms Hazel Poa of PSP is asking that Parliament suspend Mr S Iswaran simply because they feel that he does not warrant the MP’s allowance, then does this mean that they have already judged that Mr Iswaran had committed a wrongdoing even before the details of the investigations are out?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: They are judging that Mr Iswaran had committed a wrongdoing even before the details of the investigation are out.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Surely, Mr Iswaran should be given due process and every opportunity to present his case before the Court of law if ever CPIB decides to charge him.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: And this is the basic principle behind the rule of law.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: So, with the greatest respect, if PSP is advocating this principle, then it is a very dangerous principle.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: It means that if any member of the public lodges a Police report against Mr Leong or Ms Poa or, for that matter, any other MP and the Police decides to commence investigations against them, this House would similarly have to suspend them from the service of Parliament.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: If Ms Poa or Mr Leong feels that an MP ought to be suspended from service merely because he is under investigation, let us seek advice and I think the Leader of the House has said already that this principle would then have to be applicable to all MPs in this House.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: In the 2 August Sitting, I asked Mr Leong whether it is his position that the Leader of Opposition, Mr Pritam cannot receive his salary or cannot carry out his duties in Parliament merely because he has been referred to the Police for investigation.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Mr Leong then replied that it only pertains to investigation by CPIB.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: As the Leader of the House said, "Why not for other offences, other serious offences – molest, rape, murder" or is it purely an arbitrary decision made by PSP?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: So, allow me to ask Mr Leong again – if an MP is investigated for perjury, for lying under oath, is that not a serious offence, too?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: It involves an allegation of dishonest conduct, an allegation of lying under oath which means that we cannot trust that person who may lie at any opportunity.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Is Ms Poa or Mr Leong saying that these offences are not serious?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: While I may not agree with Mr Pritam Singh on some political matters, I will stand to defend his right to sit in Parliament unless he is convicted of an offence and, even then, the punishment levied must be such that it will disqualify him from serving as an MP under the Constitution, because not every punishment will result in disqualification as an MP under the Constitution.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: So, the fundamental question which I have for the two NCMPs is: what is their basis for asking for Mr Iswaran to be suspended from service when we do not even know what is the case against him?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: He has been placed on leave of absence and, hence, is not able to attend Parliament.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: So, I do not understand this rush to suspend him.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Why not allow the CPIB time to do its work?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Does PSP say that every single Government officer who is under investigation for any offence also be suspended, and the salary docked?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Why would PSP want Parliament to amend an Act of Parliament just simply to push for the suspension of salary of one particular MP?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I think Mr Lim actually used the wrong word here.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: The first is the legal principle of the presumption of innocence, which have been mentioned by the Leader of the Opposition and Mr Lim.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: The second is the legal and democratic principle of tenure of office as provided in the Constitution.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: The first is a simple, almost universal principle that where a person is being investigated or has been charged with an offence, he is to be presumed innocent until found guilty by a court of law.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: The Government's stated position is equivocal support for this principle.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: As the hon Minister for Law said in response to the hon Member Christopher de Souza's Parliamentary Question on this in August 2008, I quote, "Let there not be any doubt on this point.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: The presumption of innocence is an important and fundamental principle, and it is one of the foundations of our criminal justice system.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: The Government is absolutely committed to upholding the presumption of innocence as a core principle in our commitment to the rule of law." The principle is also applied by the Courts in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: In a judgment by then Justice VK Raja, also in 2008, His Honour wrote, "If the evidence is insufficient to support the prosecution's theory of guilt, the judge must acquit the accused... it simply has not been proved to the satisfaction of the law that the accused is guilty, and the presumption of innocence stands unrebutted." As it stands, Minister Iswaran is still under investigation.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: No charges have been brought at this point and no determination has been made by a Court.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: Therefore, the presumption of innocence continues to stand unrebutted.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: The second principle is that of tenure of office.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: Article 46(1) of the Constitution provides that an MP will continue to be an MP from the time of election until the next dissolution of Parliament.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: The principle of tenure of an MP is important.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: It is a nod to the fact that MPs are elected by the people, who are the highest source of authority in a democracy and that they should therefore not be easily removable by any other authority in the land.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: This underlying reason should also apply to suspensions because the suspension is imposed by a body other than the people and prevents an MP from carrying out what he was elected to do.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: It should therefore not be a lever that is easily available and should only be used under very narrow circumstances.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: Suspension is provided for in sections 21(1)C and 21(2) of the Parliament (Privileges, Immunities and Powers) Act 1962.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: The narrow circumstances in which it may be invoked is where the MP has displayed dishonourable conduct, abuse of privilege or contempt.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: As regard abuse of privilege, an MP must be first found guilty of abuse of privilege.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: As regards contempt, the MP must first have had to be found to have committed contempt by a Select Committee or found guilty in a court of law, pursuant to prosecution by the Public Prosecutor, or if an MP was summarily determined by Parliament to be guilty if the alleged offence was committed in the view of Parliament or where it was Sitting.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: The Standing Orders (SOs) also provide for suspension of a Member.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: SO59 provides that Parliament may suspend a Member but specifically so for the commission of the offences of disregarding the authority of the Chair or of persistently and wilfully obstructing the business of Parliament by abusing the rules of Parliament.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: Such a suspension requires that a vote be put to Parliament to determine whether such an offence had actually been committed.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: If I may read that out, "Nothing in this Standing Order shall be taken to deprive Parliament of the power of proceeding against any Member according to any resolution of Parliament." This does not mean that Parliament has the ability or the right to willy nilly decide to pass resolutions and to suspend Members for any reason.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: These resolutions must be pursuant to one of the provisions that I had mentioned earlier.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: So, the common thread through all of these prescribed potential avenues for the suspension of an MP is that it must have been judged or determined in the manner provided that an offence had actually been committed.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: In the current matter involving Minister Iswaran, the case is still under investigation.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: No judgment or determination has been arrived at.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: I therefore come back to what I started with.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: In this regard, I cannot support the Motion by the hon NCMP.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: I will support the Motion by the hon Minister Indranee Rajah.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: As a final point, Sir, I would like to confess that unlike Mr Lim, who was disturbed by it, when I first saw the Motion, as a graduate in both political science and law, I was quite titillated by this question of the circumstances in which an elected MP could be removed, suspended or otherwise prevented from exercising the mandate given to him by voters.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: I listened very carefully to Ms Poa's speech to identify the legal leg upon which her Motion would stand – but there was none.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: The matter involving Minister Iswaran has understandably created anxiousness and some amount of consternation amongst the public.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: As a polity that prices transparency, fairness and incorruptibility, it is not unexpected that questions on egalitarian treatment or just or unjust remuneration have a reason in relation to this case.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: But Parliament operates within the constructs created by the Constitution, by law and by our SOs.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: Whether it is to do with the suspension of a Member, formalities like Points of Order, apologies or Guillotine Times for Budget Cuts, or larger questions like how to ensure free and fair debate in this Chamber, there are laws, rules and procedures that apply to all of us.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: If a Member disagrees with these constructs or thinks that there are better ways to do things, then it is open to that Member to propose to amend them and for Parliament to consider these proposed amendments.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: But as long as these provisions stand, they must be abided by, and Motions, Debates and proposals must be framed within them.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: It is not a licence to proceed to do something outside the constructs of the law in a knee-jerk reaction.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: And as difficult as it may be in a public justice system where accused persons are publicly mentioned, we must maintain the presumption of innocence until proven guilty.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: So, Mr Speaker, Sir, while I was titillated by the academic idea of the Motion, I was deeply disappointed in the substance of it.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: A Motion that calls for the suspension of a Member must necessarily as a basic premise first set out the legal provisions upon which the proposed suspension would stand.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: There were simply none disclosed in Ms Poa's speech.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: I also disagree with the Motion standing in the name of Ms Hazel Poa calling for the suspension of Mr Iswaran until the end of this term of Parliament.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Our role as an MP, Mr Speaker, ultimately comes from the mandates at the ballot box.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: It should therefore not be taken away lightly.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: An MP is not an employee but, rather, is self-employed.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Being an MP gives a person certain privileges, including the right to attend and speak in Parliament.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Related to this, while an MP is self-employed, when an MP is elected on a party platform, that MP is also accountable to the party and the party's rules.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Ultimately, the party is also, in turn, accountable to the electorate.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: So, if a party puts a Member on leave of absence, that party would ultimately be accountable to the electorate to ensure that the electorate continues to be served.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: These are all mechanisms that includes checks and balances within themselves.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: I do not think any of these accusations are currently being made in this Motion against Mr Iswaran.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: The subsequent sections such as section 21 of PIPPA set out the process for making determinations.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: I would add that generally, fair process should be accorded to a Member before his privileges are suspended.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Ms Poa seems to agree with this principle and acknowledges that ultimately, this is a matter that will be determined by the investigation process and, if necessary, by a Court thereafter.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Generally, fair process includes the Member being made aware of the allegations against him and being given a chance to answer it.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: So, if Parliament wishes to exercise punitive powers before investigation is concluded, then that Member should be given a chance to answer those allegations.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Clearly, I would suggest that in this case, that would not be appropriate because Mr Iswaran is being investigated by CPIB.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: It would be a bit of a circus for a second investigation to take place in Parliament over the exact same set of facts.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Where there has been no determination that Mr Iswaran has committed any crimes or engaged in dishonourable conduct, I would suggest that the punitive powers of Parliament should not be exercised yet.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: In general, a person is presumed to be innocent until he has been convicted, and Mr Iswaran should be accorded the same right as every other person has.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: The SOs of Parliament have one provision dealing with the suspension of a Member and this is SO59.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: I think Ms Poa referred to SO59(5), which says that nothing in this Order will take away the general powers of Parliament to suspend the Member.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: What is interesting is SO59 is actually an Order that deals with the powers of the Speaker to propose a suspension of a Member: one, for disregard for the authority of the Chair; or two, persistently and wilfully obstructing the business of Parliament.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: These are the only express grounds in the SOs of Parliament that allow for the suspension of a Member.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: While these provisions have been used by Speakers in some other jurisdictions, in Singapore, I am not aware of any case where this power has been used to suspend a Member.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: So, I would suggest that if we are going to stray outside of these express provisions that give Parliament the power to suspend the Member, we have to be crystal clear on the principles being applied.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: It also goes against the principle of retrospective criminality for us to see what has happened and then decide that is wrong.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: It is important for laws to set out very clearly what is wrong first so that people know what standards they have to abide by.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: If you look at this Motion objectively, what is happening here is, if you just look at the facts, I think Ms Poa was Mr Iswaran's opponent in the West Coast Group Representation Constituency and has now put up a Motion calling for his suspension.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: If this is set as a precedent, imagine what this power would do on the opposite side, if a ruling party were to decide it wants to suspend a Member without any clear, principled basis.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Those Motions would pass if the Party Whip were exercised.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Clearly, that would not be a precedent we want to set.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: So, I would suggest that Members be very, very slow to put forward Motions calling for the suspension of another Member, especially where there has been no clear, principled basis for this.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Related to this, Ms Poa is proposing an amendment to PPIPA, which is legislation.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Generally, legislation is meant to address the country at large and is not meant to be targeted at an individual or a particular case.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: It would actually be quite unprincipled to amend legislation for a single case.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I will now call on Leader of the House to make her reply on her Motion on "Consideration of Matters Regarding Member of Parliament", followed by Ms Hazel for her reply on her Motion on "Suspension of Member".

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Thereafter, I will put the question in respect of each Motion to the House for voting.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Leader of the House, you have up to 40 minutes.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I would like now to respond to what has been said by Ms Hazel Poa and the position of PSP, but also to help Members understand the principles and the tenets upon which we should act in such a situation.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Insofar as Ms Poa and PSP's position is concerned, what does concern me greatly, is that her Motion and the move to suspend Minister Iswaran does not appear to come from a place of principle.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: It is, by her own admission, specifically targeted at Minister Iswaran and not a matter of policy or principle.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: In order to decide what we must do for this, it is very important to first understand what the law is.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And that is why I asked Ms Poa under which specific provision she was seeking to suspend Mr Iswaran.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Because as I understood her argument, which is the same as she has posted on social media, her argument, PSP's argument is that: "I want to cut your pay.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And because I want to cut your pay, I want to suspend you." In other words, "this is the result I want, and therefore, I would suspend you." But that is not the correct approach, because when you look at our rules, you will see that generally, suspension is a punishment.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And the cutting of pay is a consequence.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, we must first ask ourselves: in what scenario do you suspend and has that threshold been met?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The PPIPA does have specific provisions on suspension.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But that begs the question: when are you suspended?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But that does not apply in this case.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: If subsequently something arises out of the investigations that you can say constitutes dishonourable conduct or abuse of privilege, then maybe so, but that has to be considered down the road.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But, at this point in time, can we say that section 20 has been triggered?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Then, there is the next provision, which is section 19.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Section 19 says, "without prejudice to sections 20 and 21, Parliament may, in accordance with its Standing Orders, suspend any Member from the service of Parliament for the remainder of the current session or for any part thereof".

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Section 19 tells you to look at the SOs.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And that is why I asked Ms Poa the question earlier.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Whatever else one may wish to accuse Mr Iswaran of, we certainly cannot accuse him of the conduct listed out in SO59.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: There may be others who may have offended that SO, but not Mr Iswaran.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: That brings us to the provision that Ms Poa referred us to earlier, which is SO59(5).

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Should this House do something just because it can?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The question is not, "should we do it because we can" and even then, I have to put a reservation there, because I am not sure that it can be read as broadly as Ms Poa puts it.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But for the sake of argument and just for the sake of argument, if it is as broad as she says, as a Parliament and as a House, we have to act on principle.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Because if we do not, it becomes very dangerous.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Because, what it then means is that we can pass any resolution that we like without having regard to values, principles or standards and targeted specifically at any Member of this House.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Think about what kind of Parliament that would be.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: What would be the standards of integrity of such a Parliament?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: What would be the sense of fairness and how would people regard this House if we did something like that?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, I would be very, very cautious before we say that we suspend a Member just because we can.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: It is quite important that we should establish the principles of suspension.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: When I asked Ms Poa what are the principles she is advocating, she listed a few.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: First, she said it is because Mr Iswaran is under investigation for corruption and corruption is a serious offence.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But then I ask Ms Poa, what about rape?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: If a Member is under investigation for those offences, should the Member be suspended?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: She said she had not thought about that, which means that she had not thought about the principle.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: This is worrying because it means that when PSP advocates something, they are not acting as a matter of principle, but as a matter of targeting a specific individual and that is my concern.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And anyway, in any event, whilst Mr Iswaran is under investigation under the Prevention of Corruption Act, firstly, it has not yet been established whether he has done any wrongdoing yet, at this point of time.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, as I mentioned before, the facts are not known, the specific allegations against him are not known.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The next thing Ms Poa said was that we should suspend because Mr Iswaran is on leave of absence.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: If that were so, then we would have to suspend Mr Faisal Manap.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: He was on leave of absence because he was ill.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But we do not do that, because he was ill.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, in other words, it is not the leave of absence in and of itself.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, as a matter of proper, good order, he should be on leave of absence.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Then, the next point that she made was because he was under arrest.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Well, yes, when you are under investigation, part of Police procedure is that you are under arrest, but I come back to the same point.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: This is still at the investigative stage, and you have not actually established whether there was any wrongdoing.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, then she made the next point that he was not performing his duties.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Here, let me just make a very short digression to say that while he has not been able to perform his duties as an MP, his constituents are still being looked after.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I wanted to make that point because it is very important that his constituents know that they are still being taken care of and are in good hands.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: In fact, Minister Desmond Lee has been doing the Meet-the-People session.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: He and another MP, I think Miss Rachel Ong, have been doing house visits.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The other MPs in West Coast GRC have been covering events on the ground.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, I just wanted the residents of West Coast GRC to know that notwithstanding the fact that Mr Iswaran has to be on leave of absence, they are still being taken care of.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Then, Ms Poa talked about the question that, well, it is taxpayers' money that is being used in the interim period.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But the important question is – what is the principle?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: You do not suspend somebody just because you do not want to pay him.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: You have to suspend him because there is a principle that has been breached or a threshold has been crossed.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And on this, I note that the Leader of the Opposition had also taken a similar position, for which I do thank him.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Because he said Parliament should be very mindful of suspending somebody in the meantime and this would set a precedent should the Government decide to fix anybody.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: He also talked about the wheels of justice and that we must not do anything precipitously – this is not the Leader of the Opposition's words – but essentially, what he is really saying, which is the same thing as what others have said is, "do not pre-judge the issue".

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And that is correct, because the Leader of the Opposition and Mr Faisal Manap are under investigation.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: On that, I just also want to say that when you look at the way that we approach that, we did not suspend them because we felt that it was better for the outcome to be heard.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: In fact, we went further in that case.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Because here, in this Motion, I am only asking for us to wait till the outcome of the investigations.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And what the Committee of Privileges said in their recommendation was this: "Based on the evidence before this Committee, we are satisfied Mr Singh had told untruths to this Committee.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Parliament is empowered to summarily decide on the matter and also decide on the appropriate sanctions based on our findings.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The specific offence in that case was dishonourable conduct and contempt.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: That falls squarely within section 20 of the PPIPA.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The Committee of Privileges had made its finding with regard to Mr Singh and Mr Faisal Manap.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Mr Singh and Mr Faisal Manap, of course, dispute that.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And that was the reason why we said they should go to Public Prosecutor.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But the Committee of Privileges and this House would have been well within its rights to say: "We accept the findings of the COP   and we act immediately under section 20." But we did not.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We did not because we felt that, as a matter of fairness, we should wait and see what the outcome of the proceedings were.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And so, the actual resolution which I moved was this: "that Mr Pritam Singh's, Ms Sylvia Lim's and Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap's respective roles as set out in the report, in relation to the untruth spoken by Ms Raeesah Khan in Parliament, and Ms Lim's or Mr Faisal's stating of untruth to the Committee on oath or affirmation and the appropriate sanctions in respect thereof, be deferred until the conclusion of the investigations and criminal proceedings, if any, against Mr Singh." So, in that case, I went further, and I said to wait till not just the conclusion of the investigations but the conclusion of the proceedings.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: In this case, I am saying, let us wait until the conclusion or the outcome of the investigations because that would put this House in a better position to know what to do.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Mr Singh supports the position that Mr Iswaran should not be suspended at this point in time, I think.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: His second question, though, was, what should Parliament do in the interim period.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And I think his position was that it might be appropriate to suspend his MP allowance.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: That is what I think Mr Singh said.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: If the Member is suspended, then he does not get any allowance.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, the law does not provide for anything in between.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Ms Poa mentioned that she had, in the original Motion, wanted to provide for clawback but was advised by Parliament – which I think is the current position under the law, that there is no provision for a clawback.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, the question is: what do we do?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Currently, right now, given the state of the law and given that we do not know the facts and that we do not know the outcome of the investigation, that is why I have said we should wait till the outcome of the investigation.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Then, we have a clearer idea of what to do.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And the next question then is, what should we then do with respect to the monies that are paid with respect to Mr Iswaran.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We will look at it again when we know if the Attorney-General's Chambers (AGC) intends to bring any charges and if so, what the charges are.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Bear in mind, this is a party discipline matter.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And the Prime Minister would do this on the basis that he has not lived up to the party discipline and standards of conduct, whether or not he has committed offences.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And if it is really necessary, then we will consider what to do with respect to legislation.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: That is the reason why I say, again, that these are issues that should be considered when the outcome of the investigation is known.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Because it may very well be that at the end of the investigation, he is also cleared.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And if he is cleared, then what we would have done in the meantime, if we accept Ms Poa's Motion, is that we would have suspended him and we would have docked his pay when there was, in fact, no need to.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: At the end of the day, it is a question of where is the balance, what is a fair way of dealing with this, given the current state of the law, given the current state of knowledge that we have?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Ms Poa's approach is, really, let us just ignore whether or not he has done anything wrong.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Let us just suspend him because it is a matter of money.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And then, if need be, we pay it back.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But I think we need to approach it as a matter of principle, which is that, at the current time, when you cannot say clearly that some threshold has been crossed, then we say wait, see what the outcome of the investigations are.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And if, depending on the outcome, a threshold has been crossed, then we will certainly look at it as a matter of party discipline.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And the Prime Minister has very firm views on standards of integrity and conduct, and he will not let the matter rest if thresholds have been crossed.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I think that assurance I can give, which is that if certain thresholds had been crossed and if warranted and merited, we will do something.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, I hope that sets Members' minds at rest, because if we do not suspend him today, it does not mean that you cannot do so in the future.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: If you do suspend him today, you are effectively saying that he has done something wrong, when there is no basis at the present time.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: There may well be later; we do not know.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But at the present time, it will be premature and prejudging the issue.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I will now invite Ms Hazel Poa to make your reply on your Motion.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Ms Hazel Poa, hold on for a while.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: My suggestion to my colleagues, Ms Poa and Mr Leong is that they have gotten it completely wrong.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: If you look at the SOs, the only relevant SO is SO59.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: It does not give you a substantive power.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: And the carefully drafted SO59 is also irrelevant.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: I do not know if you have understood how the provisions work together.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: I would suggest you go and read it carefully before Ms Poa concludes.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: As I have said, you have also up to 40 minutes.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: All of us share a common desire to maintain high standards of conduct in this House and to treat Members who are under investigation firmly and fairly.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: These are motherhood statements that few are expected to disagree with.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: How we apply such standards, however, may not be the same.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Such differences will come to the fore when we apply them to specific cases, like in the case of Minister Iswaran.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: While PSP feels that it is fair to suspend Minister Iswaran for now and to back pay him when he is cleared of all wrongdoing, the Leader of the House does not think so.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This amendment gives Parliament the flexibility to decide whether suspended Members should be paid their allowance, whether in full or in part.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Without this flexibility, Parliament is hampered in taking timely disciplinary actions.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: If we are unable to back pay and we have to uphold the principle of innocence until proven guilty, it means that we cannot suspend any Member until the entire legal process has been completed.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This may be a long period of time.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We are, in fact, being held ransom due to the lack of provision to back pay.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Regardless of Parliament's decision on Minister Iswaran, we believe that the amendment should still be passed.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: There is only an upside, no downsides to this amendment.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I think the common theme that runs throughout is the presumption of innocence.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: All who spoke – Mr Lim Biow Chuan, Mr Raj Joshua Thomas and Mr Vikram Nair – made the same point that by suspending, we are presuming that he is guilty.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I think that argument is a red herring.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: If suspension means presumption of guilt, then I am afraid we have been doing that on many, many occasions.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Police officers have been suspended from duties and placed on half pay while they are under investigations, as evident in answer to a Parliamentary Question just yesterday and the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) has also said that is a standard practice for Police officers.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: So, the fact of the matter is suspension is not a determination of guilt.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It is merely a measure that is commonly used to deal with situations where a person is under investigation.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Most of the time the suspension comes in two parts: suspension of duties and an effect on the pay.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In this particular case, the Prime Minister has already made the decision to suspend Minister Iswaran from his Ministerial duties and reduced his pay to $8,500.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: He has also suspended him from performing his MP duties and have his other colleagues cover for him in his constituency.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: All that I am asking for in this House is to suspend the allowance as well.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In addition, Members Raj Joshua Thomas and Vikram Nair also mentioned that MPs have the mandate of the people and, therefore, suspension of duties should not be lightly done.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Does this mean they have an issue with the Prime Minister's decision to suspend Minister Iswaran from his duties as an MP?

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The Leader of the House said that while section 59(5) says Parliament can suspend a Member, we should not be doing something just because we can.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I believe I made it very clear why we are asking for this.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I have also listed the three reasons why I think we have a good case to suspend Minister Iswaran.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The Leader of the House proceeded to address them one by one, but she does them in isolation.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: For example, when I said that he is not performing the duties, she quoted the example of medical leave.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: But the three conditions are meant to be taken together, not individually.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: For example, when we say that you can vote if you are a Singapore Citizen and aged 21, you do not tackle the criteria one by one, age 21 separate from Singapore Citizen.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: PSP feels that adopting a harsher stand against corruption versus other wrongdoing is fair, given the extremely high salaries we are paying Ministers to stay corruption-free.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Since we are paying such extraordinarily high salaries, is it not fair for the consequence of corruption and the handling process of its investigation to be correspondingly tougher?

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Adopting a light touch approach here will only send the wrong signal.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The sanguine approach adopted towards Minister Iswaran's MP allowance stands in stark contrast to the approach adopted towards the public.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: How is it equitable that Minister Iswaran gets in one month what these ComCare recipients get over three years?

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: If the investigation and prosecution take one year, the amount he continues to receive will be equivalent to what these ComCare recipients get over 38 years.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: PSP urges the House to suspend Minister Iswaran and to back pay him if and when he is cleared of all wrongdoing.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We have explained why our approach leads to better use of taxpayers' money while making sure that Minister Iswaran is not penalised should he be found innocent.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This is in line with our idea of being firm and fair.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We trust that all who have been following this debate are well able to come to their own conclusions.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Just a quick clarification for the Leader on the status of Mr S Iswaran's responsibilities as an MP.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I have asked two questions specifically on his access to MPAS, for example, his access to Government buildings, including Parliament.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Sorry, I just want to make sure that I have the question correct.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: One was access to Government buildings and the other was?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Can I trouble Mr Singh to repeat the question?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: The other question was access to the Public Service Division’s (PSD) Member of Parliament Appeal System (MPAS).

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Essentially, just to confirm whether the Minister is still performing his roles and duties on the ground as an MP looking after his constituents.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Because I think the key issue here is, if he is effectively suspended as an MP as well?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: As a Minister, he was appointed by the Prime Minister.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, he holds that position at the Prime Minister's pleasure.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The Prime Minister, therefore, also has the ability to interdict him and to tell him to stop carrying out duties as Minister whilst he is under investigation.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: That is because his appointment flowed or came from the Prime Minister.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: That flows from the Ministerial position; and that is obviously because you are under investigation, and you do not want to prejudice the investigation.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Then, there is the issue of Mr Iswaran's status as an MP.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Mr Iswaran's status as an MP was not by appointment, by the Prime Minister or otherwise.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: He was elected by the constituents of West Coast GRC.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And I have taken Members through those provisions.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Imagine if he was sitting here and somebody were to ask him about the investigation, what is he going to say?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I mean, the investigative authorities are listening to this.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: He might end up jeopardising his own case.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, as a matter of party discipline and good order, he has been asked to stay away and, at least to his credit, he has complied with that – even though he is entitled to come in as an MP.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: That is why I think I should also clarify something which was said earlier by Ms Poa, which I think I have just clarified by my explanation.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I think Ms Poa said something to the effect of Mr Iswaran being suspended by the Prime Minister.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Anyway, the direction to stop work as a Minister – the interdiction – comes from the Prime Minister in his capacity as Prime Minister to Mr Iswaran in his capacity as a Minister.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Insofar as not carrying out MP duties and going on leave of absence, that is something which is requested by the Prime Minister as a matter of party discipline.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Mr Iswaran could come to Parliament if he wants to, but he has not done so because he has listened to what he has been asked to do.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Suspension is as provided for under the Act and certain criterion and thresholds have to be met.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: That was the clarification I wanted to make.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: When I approve your leave of absence from Parliament, you could still turn up in Parliament.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Mr Vikram Nair, did you raise your hand as well?

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: I raised my hand because Ms Poa had asked me a question on what I thought of Mr Iswaran's suspension.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: But I think the Leader has addressed that.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Any other clarifications for either Minister Indranee or Ms Poa?

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: I feel compelled to speak and seek clarification from Ms Hazel Poa as to what is her purpose and intent in comparing this amount of allowance that is still being paid until a verdict has been reached on Minister Iswaran's case, with the payouts from ComCare.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Because I believe Ms Poa as an ex-public servant knows very well that these are budgets that are completely separate from each other.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: And it does not mean that simply because you suspend an MP, that money is going to go to some further ComCare applications.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: So, I would like to clarify what is her intention in bringing up this analogy?

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: If it is not paid, it will actually be still within Government coffers that can be redirected elsewhere.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: The purpose of PSP raising this Motion is to ensure we are consistent in terms of when we are advocating high salaries for our public office holders.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Because we are advocating that high salaries will lead to being corruption-free.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: So, after we have established that, we also have to ensure that the high salaries go to deserving people.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: In this case, I am interested in what the Leader has said towards the end of her closing speech just now.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: The Leader mentioned about the possibility of clawback and we have also recommended back pay.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: The problem of our legislation today is that it does not provide for clawback or back pay of the high salaries that we are paying our public office holders.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: So, if the Leader can confirm that we are going to have a Bill in the future to ensure that that legislation is also in place, then I think PSP can reconsider many of our positions with regard to this Motion.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: First, he says that he is concerned about the salaries and, of course, what would happen in the case when somebody is not performing.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: How that is to be affected remains to be seen.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Because as explained today, the law as it currently is, does not allow for it.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: This does not, however, preclude the Prime Minister from, as a matter of party discipline, requiring it.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: What I can assure Members of is that, at least on our side – the party's side – we will do what is right and what is fair, having regard to the circumstances.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: We have now come to the conclusion of the debate.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I shall put forth the necessary questions to the House for a decision.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: We will first deal with the Motion by the Leader of the House on "Consideration of Matters Regarding Member of Parliament".

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Any Member who wishes his dissent or abstention to be recorded or to claim a Division before I declare the result, kindly stand up so we will record that.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: We will now deal with Ms Poa's Motion on "Suspension of Member".

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Does any Member wish for his dissent or abstention to be recorded or to claim a Division before I declare the result?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Ms Hazel Poa, I would like to ask whether you wish to proceed with the Bill.
